newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up but advance seen petering out.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up but advance seen petering out.

text.p: Slovenian shares continued their advance for the third consecutive day on Friday in what traders described as a technical rebound likely to run out of steam soon.

"The rebound continues as prices are still regarded as low. But I can't see any reason for a rise next week and volumes will be low because of Wednesday's holiday," said Igor Marosa, a trader of brokerage Proxy.
The SBI index rose 1.66 percent or 19.91 points to 1,220.7. Since Friday last week the blue-chip index fell 1.21 percent.
Overall 10 shares rose, three fell and two were flat, while 13 were untraded. Turnover slumped to 37.3 million tolars from 94.3 million.
"No major changes will occur before the constitution is amended and the uncertainty surrounding EU association treaty is clarified," Marosa said.

Earlier this month the constitutional court said the parliament needed to change the constitution to enable foreigners to buy land before it could ratify the association agreement with the EU, which was signed a year ago.
Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said he expected the constitution to be changed by July 15 and ratification to follow immediately.
Traders predicted the SBI index could fall by 10 to 15 percent as foreign investors would remain at bay until the two issues were solved.
"Until there is money on the table I do not believe we will see any rise. Meanwhile selling pressure from holders of shares in newly privatised companies is pushing prices down," Marosa added.
Drug maker Lek was the most actively traded share, firming 2.39 percent to 22,300 tolars on volume of 337 shares for total turnover of 7.5 million tolars.
Port operator Luka was the top gainer, jumping 2.48 percent to 1,650 tolars on volume of 510 shares.
Market participants attributed both gains to a technical correction after the losses last week and this week.
Financial consultancy Primofin PFNP.LJ, which was traded today for the first time this month, led the decliners, tumbling 10.23 percent to 11,850 tolars on volume of 10 shares.
"I don't know anybody who would be interested in this share as there are so many other shares worth buying, and volume of only 10 shares is not significant enough," one broker said.
